docs.title: vexy-vlip-js
docs.text:
vexy-vlip-js turns one video and one WebVTT file into an interactive explainer. Each WebVTT cue becomes an on-screen card: a real HTML panel with its own background, padding, corner radius, shadow and position. The library has no runtime dependencies and uses only native browser APIs.

Open the live demo Install

docs.title: What goes in, what comes out
docs.text:
You supply:

  • a video file, for example demo.mp4;
  • a WebVTT file, for example demo.vtt, whose cues hold the card text, timing and placement.

Vexy Vlip creates a <video> element, fetches and parses the WebVTT file itself, and draws each cue as an absolutely positioned card in an overlay layer above the video. The browser's own caption renderer is not used, so ::cue styling limits do not apply.

A single cue shows the idea:

WEBVTT

00:02.000 --> 00:05.000 position:70%,line-right line:24%,start size:38%
Click the **Export** button in the toolbar.

From 2 s to 5 s, a card appears whose top-right corner sits at 70 % of the video width and 24 % of its height. The card is 38 % of the video width and shows "Export" in bold.

docs.title: Two playback modes
docs.text:
Mode Behaviour continuous (default) The video plays normally. Each card appears at its cue start and disappears at its cue end. stepped The video plays to the start of the next cue, pauses, and shows that card. The viewer clicks, presses Space, or uses the in-card Next button to continue.

In stepped mode you can also set an easing such as ease-in-out. The player then moves currentTime between stops on a requestAnimationFrame loop instead of playing natively. See How playback works.

docs.title: Three ways to load it
docs.text:
Build How you use it Typical use ESM module import { VexyVlip } from "vexy-vlip-js" Bundled apps Web Component <vexy-vlip src="…" track="…"> Plain HTML pages Classic global <script src="vexy-vlip.global.js"> exposes window.VexyVlip Pages with no build step

All three share the same engine in src/player.js.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Installation: npm and CDN setup.
  • Quick start: a working player in four steps.
  • Authoring cards: plain-text cues, cue settings and JSON cards.
  • Options and attributes: every constructor option and its matching HTML attribute.
  • API reference: methods, getters, events and exported helpers.
  • Theming: CSS custom properties.
  • Live demos: the hosted example pages.

vexy-vlip-js is licensed under Apache-2.0. Source: github.com/vexyart/vexy-vlip-js.

docs.title: new VexyVlip(target, options)
docs.text:
import { VexyVlip } from "vexy-vlip-js";
const vlip = new VexyVlip(document.querySelector("#stage"), { src, track });
  • target is a container element. The player adds the class vexy-vlip, a <video> element, the card layer and the controls inside it.
  • If target is a <video> element, the player wraps it in a new <div>, uses that <div> as the container, and keeps the existing video.
  • If target is missing or not a DOM element, the constructor throws TypeError("VexyVlip: a target element is required").
  • options is described in Options and attributes.

The constructor returns at once. The track loads asynchronously, and the player is ready when both the video metadata and the cards are loaded. Wait for the vexyvlip:ready event, or check the ready getter, before relying on segments.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Method Description play() Continuous: play. Stepped: advance to the next stop. On the Start/Replay screen it acts like the button. pause() Pause and cancel any eased travel. toggle() Continuous: play or pause. Stepped: advance when paused, pause while travelling. next() Stepped: advance to the next card. Continuous: seek to the next cue start. prev() Go to the previous card and show it. close() Dismiss the cards: switch to continuous mode and resume playback. No effect in continuous mode. replay() Restart from the beginning, like the Replay button. seekTo(time) Seek to an absolute time in seconds (negative values become 0). goToSegment(i) Pause at the start of card i, show it, and dismiss the Start/Replay screen. Ignored if i does not exist. setMode(mode) Switch between "continuous" and "stepped" while running. Stepping resumes from the card the playhead rests on. setEasing(easing) Change the easing. Unknown names are ignored. showCard(i) / hideCard() Show or hide a card manually. getSegments() A copy of the parsed card models. destroy() Remove the player's DOM, listeners and frame callbacks.

docs.title: Getters
docs.text: Getter Value segments Deep copy of the parsed card models. currentSegment Index of the visible card; if none is visible, the last cue start at or before the playhead, or -1. currentTime The video's current time in seconds. duration The video's duration in seconds. mode "continuous" or "stepped". playing true while the video plays or eased travel is running. ready true once metadata and cards are loaded.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
Every event is a CustomEvent named vexyvlip:<name>, dispatched on the player container. Events bubble and are composed, so events from <vexy-vlip> cross its shadow root and reach the host element.

Event detail When vexyvlip:ready { segments } (card count) Metadata and cards are loaded. vexyvlip:play {} Playback or a stepped advance starts. vexyvlip:pause {} pause() ran. vexyvlip:ended {} The video reached its end. vexyvlip:segmententer { index, segment } A card's segment became active. vexyvlip:segmentexit { index } Stepped mode left a card. vexyvlip:cardshow { index, segment } A card appeared. vexyvlip:cardhide {} or { index } A card disappeared. vexyvlip:stop { index } Stepped mode reached a stop point. vexyvlip:modechange { mode } setMode() changed the mode. vexyvlip:close {} The × dropped the player into plain video mode. vexyvlip:replay {} Replay restarted playback. vexyvlip:destroy {} destroy() ran. vexyvlip:error { error, phase } phase is "track" when the track download failed, "play" when video.play() was rejected. 
stage.addEventListener("vexyvlip:cardshow", (e) => {
  console.log("card", e.detail.index, e.detail.segment.text);
});

You can also pass a callback option instead of a listener: onReady, onCardshow, onStop and so on. The player calls it with (detail, player).

docs.title: Keyboard shortcuts
docs.text:
With keyboard: true (the default), the player root handles these keys:

Key Action Space / Enter toggle(): advance or play/pause Right next() Left prev() F Toggle full screen M Toggle mute

docs.title: The <vexy-vlip> element
docs.text:
Importing vexy-vlip-js/element, dist/vexy-vlip.element.js or the global build registers <vexy-vlip> once (it is skipped if the name is already defined). The element:

  • renders the player inside an open shadow root with its own stylesheet;
  • adopts a child <video> element if you provide one;
  • exposes the same methods (play, pause, toggle, next, prev, close, replay, seekTo, goToSegment, showCard, hideCard, getSegments, setMode, setEasing, destroy) and getters;
  • adds a player getter that returns the internal VexyVlip instance;
  • implements setMode() and setEasing() by setting the mode and easing attributes;
  • destroys the player when removed from the document.

docs.title: The global build
docs.text: vexy-vlip.global.js is an IIFE. It sets window.VexyVlip to the class, adds VexyVlip.Element (the custom element class) and VexyVlip.version, and registers <vexy-vlip>.

docs.title: Pure helpers
docs.text:
src/index.js also exports the side-effect-free functions the player uses. They need no DOM, so they run under Node.js.

Export Purpose parseVtt(text) Parse WebVTT into raw cues: { index, id, start, end, settings, payload }. parseTime(stamp) Convert "MM:SS.mmm" or "HH:MM:SS.mmm" to seconds; NaN if malformed. parseCueSettings(str) Read position, line, size, align, vertical, region into an object. cueToCard(cue, defaults) Convert a raw cue into a card model. parseCards(text, defaults) parseVtt followed by cueToCard for every cue. renderMarkdown(text) Render the escaped markdown subset to HTML. stopPoints(cards) Stop table { index, time, end }, sorted by time. segmentAtTime(cards, t) Index of the card active at t, or -1. nextStop(cards, t) / prevStop(cards, t) Next or previous cue start strictly after or before t, or -1. currentStop(cards, t) Last cue start at or before t, or -1. CSS, shadowCss(), injectStyles(doc) The stylesheet string, its shadow-DOM variant, and a one-time <head> injector. DEFAULTS The default option values. version The package version string.

A card model returned by cueToCard() has these fields: index, id, start, end, text, html, isHtml, placement ({ x, y, w, anchor, align }), style ({ bg, fg, font, padding, radius, border, shadow, opacity }), className, enter and exit.

The navigation helpers compare times with a tolerance of 0.02 s (exported from src/segments.js as EPS).

docs.title: How playback works
docs.text: This page explains what the player does between loading a track and showing a card. It follows the five-cue sample.vtt used by the demos: cards start at 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 seconds.

docs.title: Source layout
docs.text: File Role src/index.js Public ESM entry. Re-exports the class and helpers; registers nothing. src/player.js The VexyVlip class: DOM, loading, both playback modes, eased travel, Start/Replay screen, events. src/vtt.js Pure WebVTT parsing and cue-to-card conversion. No DOM. src/segments.js Pure stop-point navigation: nextStop, prevStop, currentStop, segmentAtTime. src/cards.js Builds card elements and applies placement and inline styles. src/styles.js The stylesheet as a string, for the shadow root or one <head> injection. src/element.js The <vexy-vlip> custom element. src/global.js Entry for the classic-script IIFE build.

docs.title: Loading
docs.text:
1. The constructor merges your options over DEFAULTS, creates the <video>, the card layer, the controls and the Start/Replay screen, and attaches listeners.
  2. If vtt is empty and track is set, the player downloads the track with fetch(). A failed request emits vexyvlip:error with phase: "track".
  3. The text goes through parseCards(), which produces one card model per cue.
  4. When both the video metadata and the cards are in, the player is ready. It applies startSegment or startAt, emits vexyvlip:ready, and either starts playback (continuous mode with autoplay), opens on the start segment, or shows the Start screen over the dimmed first frame.

docs.title: The frame loop
docs.text: While the video plays, the player checks the playhead once per frame. It uses video.requestVideoFrameCallback() where the browser supports it, and requestAnimationFrame() otherwise. Only one callback is queued at a time.

docs.title: Continuous mode
docs.text:
On each frame the player calls segmentAtTime(cards, currentTime). When the result changes, it shows the new card (segmententer, cardshow) or hides the old one (cardhide). Playback is never paused for a card.

With sample.vtt, the card for cue 1 is visible from 2.0 s to 3.5 s, then no card is visible until 4.0 s.

docs.title: Stepped mode
docs.text:
Stepped mode advances by card index, not by time, so a cue at 00:00.000 and back-to-back cues each get their own stop.

  1. The viewer advances (click, Space, Next, or next()). The current card hides and the player emits segmentexit and cardhide.
  2. The target is the start of the next card. With sample.vtt, resting on card 0 (2 s) gives a target of 4 s.
  3. With easing: "linear" the video plays natively. On each frame the player checks currentTime + 0.02 >= target, stopping slightly early to avoid overshoot.
  4. At the stop the player pauses, snaps currentTime to exactly the cue start, shows the card, and emits segmententer, cardshow and stop.
  5. After the last card, the next advance plays to the end of the video. The player emits ended and shows the Replay screen.

prev() goes back by one index and shows that card immediately, with no playback.

docs.title: Eased travel
docs.text:
When easing is ease-in, ease-out or ease-in-out, stepped advances do not use native playback:

  1. The video pauses and is muted, because scrubbed audio is unusable.

  2. A requestAnimationFrame loop sets currentTime from the current stop to the target. The trip takes (target − start) / playbackRate seconds of wall time, and progress is mapped through the curve:

    Easing Curve f(p) linear p ease-in p² ease-out 1 − (1 − p)² ease-in-out p² (3 − 2p) (smoothstep)

  3. At the target the original mute state is restored and the stop is handled as in step 4 above.

Eased travel depends on fast seeking. Encode the video with fast-start and a short GOP; see Installation.

docs.title: Card placement
docs.text: A card model's placement holds x, y, an optional w, an anchor and an align. The card element is positioned at (x, y) inside the video box and shifted with a CSS transform so the chosen anchor point of the card lands on that position. Numbers are percentages; strings are used as CSS lengths.

docs.title: Why not the native caption renderer
docs.text: The browser's ::cue pseudo-element cannot set arbitrary backgrounds, padding, radius, shadows or exact placement, and its cues are not regular DOM. Vexy Vlip renders each cue as an ordinary element instead: the card layer is an aria-live="polite" region and each card has role="note", so screen readers announce new cards.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: The project's specification limits it to one sentence: play one video, drive styled HTML cards from its WebVTT track, and let the viewer step through the video card by card or watch it continuously, using native browser APIs only. Transcoding, adaptive streaming, analytics and editing are out of scope.

docs.title: Authoring cards
docs.text: The WebVTT file is both the script and the layout. Each cue's timing decides when its card appears, and its payload and cue settings decide what the card says and where it sits. A cue payload is either plain text or a JSON object.

docs.title: How the parser reads a file
docs.text:
The player fetches the track and parses it with parseVtt() in src/vtt.js, not with the browser's <track> renderer.

  • The file is split into blocks on blank lines. Windows line endings and a leading byte-order mark are normalised.
  • The WEBVTT header block is skipped. NOTE, STYLE and REGION blocks are skipped entirely.
  • An optional cue identifier line (such as step-1) may precede the timing line. It becomes the card's id.
  • Timestamps are MM:SS.mmm or HH:MM:SS.mmm. A comma is also accepted as the decimal separator. A cue with a malformed timestamp is dropped.
  • Every line after the timing line is the payload. A WebVTT cue cannot contain a blank line, so a payload is one run of non-empty lines.

docs.title: Plain-text cards
docs.text:
00:02.000 --> 00:05.000 position:70%,line-right line:24%,start size:38%
Click the **Export** button in the toolbar.

docs.title: Placement with cue settings
docs.text:
All values are percentages of the video box.

Setting Effect position:N%[,line-left\|center\|line-right] Horizontal pin. The optional position-align picks which edge or the centre of the card sits at that point. line:N%[,start\|center\|end] Vertical pin. The optional line-align picks the edge: start is the top, end is the bottom. size:N% Card width as a percentage of the video width. align:start\|center\|end Text alignment. It is also the default position-align when that is omitted. left and right are read as start and end.

The position-align and line-align values combine into one of nine anchor points. For example, line-right with end gives bottom-right, and center with start gives top. When a cue has a position but no line, the card sits at the bottom. When a cue has no placement settings at all, the card is centred horizontally (x = 50 %) with its bottom edge at 88 % of the height.

The parser also reads vertical and region, but cards are always laid out horizontally.

Worked example: position:70%,line-right line:24%,start size:38% pins the card's top-right corner (line-right + start = top-right) at 70 % across and 24 % down, and makes the card 38 % of the video width.

docs.title: Markdown in card text
docs.text:
Card text is HTML-escaped first, so raw HTML never survives. Then a markdown subset is rendered:

  • inline: **bold**, *italic*, `code`, ~~strike~~, [label](url);
  • block: # to ###### headings, -/*/+ bulleted lists, 1. numbered lists, and --- horizontal rules;
  • consecutive plain lines join into one paragraph with line breaks.

Links whose target starts with javascript:, data: or vbscript: are replaced with #. A single plain line is rendered without a <p> wrapper.

docs.title: JSON cards
docs.text:
A cue whose trimmed payload starts with { is parsed as JSON. Use it for per-card styling or trusted HTML. If the JSON does not parse, the payload is shown as plain text, so a typo never produces a blank card.

00:05.000 --> 00:08.000
{ "text": "Drag the slider to fan the cards out.",
  "x": 8, "y": 62, "w": 36, "anchor": "top-left",
  "bg": "#10243a", "fg": "#eaf2ff", "radius": 14, "padding": "14px 18px",
  "shadow": "0 8px 30px rgba(0,0,0,.45)", "class": "tip" }

docs.title: JSON fields
docs.text:
Every field is optional, but give one of text or html.

Field Type Default Notes text string — Plain text with the markdown subset. html string — Trusted HTML. Filtered only when the sanitize option is on. x number or string derived Horizontal anchor. A number is a percentage of the width; a string is a CSS length. y number or string derived Vertical anchor. A number is a percentage of the height. w number or string auto Card width. anchor enum bottom Which point of the card sits at (x, y): top-left, top, top-right, left, center, right, bottom-left, bottom, bottom-right. align enum start Text alignment inside the card. bg string theme Card background: any CSS colour or gradient. fg string theme Text colour. font string theme CSS font shorthand or family. padding string theme CSS padding. radius number or string theme Border radius. border string theme CSS border. shadow string theme CSS box-shadow. opacity number 1 Applied to a solid bg colour only. class string — Extra class names for your own CSS. enter / exit enum fade Per-card transition: fade, slide-up, slide-down, none.

Placement priority is: JSON x/y/w/anchor, then the cue's own position/line/size, then the default (bottom-centre at y = 88 %). An unknown anchor value falls back to bottom.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Treat the WebVTT file as trusted content

Plain-text cards and JSON text cards are always HTML-escaped. A JSON html card is inserted as-is. With sanitize: true the player removes <script>, <style>, <iframe>, <object> and <embed> elements, on* attributes, and href/src values starting with javascript:. This is a convenience filter, not a hardened sanitiser: it does not cover data: URLs, srcdoc, SVG <use>, formaction or CSS url(). For untrusted input, sanitise upstream with a vetted library such as DOMPurify.

docs.title: Checking a track without a browser
docs.text:
The parser is pure JavaScript, so you can inspect a track under Node.js:

import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { parseCards } from "vexy-vlip-js";

const cards = parseCards(readFileSync("demo.vtt", "utf8"));
for (const c of cards) console.log(c.start, c.end, c.placement.anchor, c.text);

parseCards() returns one card model per cue. See API reference for the model's fields.

docs.title: Live demos
docs.text:
The demo pages are plain HTML files published next to this documentation. Each loads the bundles built from the current source.

Page Build used What it shows Demo landing page vexy-vlip.global.js A nine-card stepped tour of the Vexy Playlines editor, with buttons to switch mode and easing and to restart. ESM module vexy-vlip.element.js, imported as a module The class driven from JavaScript with Prev, Play/advance, Next and mode buttons, plus an event log. Web Component vexy-vlip.global.js A <vexy-vlip> element in stepped mode with ease-in-out travel. Classic global vexy-vlip.global.js window.VexyVlip used from a classic <script>.

docs.title: Media used by the demos
docs.text:
File Content media/sample.mp4 Short test clip. media/sample.vtt Five cues mixing plain-text and JSON cards. media/playlines.mp4 Screen recording of the Vexy Playlines editor. media/playlines.vtt Nine cues placed with WebVTT cue settings only, no JSON.

These are copies of the files in the repository's testdata/ folder.

docs.title: Using the hosted bundles
docs.text:
The bundles on this site are unversioned:

  • https://vexy.dev/vexy-vlip-js/vexy-vlip.element.js
  • https://vexy.dev/vexy-vlip-js/vexy-vlip.global.js

They change whenever the site is rebuilt, so use them for experiments only. For production pages load a pinned version from jsDelivr or unpkg, as shown in Installation.

docs.title: Running the demos locally
docs.text:
Prerequisites: Node.js and a clone of the repository.

  1. Install the development dependencies:

    npm install

  2. Build the bundles and copy them, with the media, into src_docs/md/:

    npm run build
npm run build:docs

  3. Start the Vite development server:

    npm run dev

  4. Open /src_docs/md/demo.html on the address Vite prints.

npm run build:docs also stamps a short content hash (?v=…) onto the bundle references in the demo pages, so browsers fetch a fresh bundle after each change.

docs.title: Development
docs.text: This page covers building, testing and releasing vexy-vlip-js from a clone of github.com/vexyart/vexy-vlip-js.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Node.js (the repository's .nvmrc pins version 20) and npm.
  • For the browser tests: Chromium for Playwright, installed with npx playwright install chromium.
  • For the documentation site: uv, which runs ProperDocs through uvx.

docs.title: npm scripts
docs.text:
Command What it does npm run dev Start the Vite development server. npm run build Two Vite passes: VEXY_BUILD=element writes dist/vexy-vlip.element.js (ES module that registers <vexy-vlip>), then VEXY_BUILD=global writes dist/vexy-vlip.global.js (IIFE that sets window.VexyVlip). Both with source maps. npm run preview vite preview. npm run test:unit node --test: pure-logic tests in tests/*.test.js for the parser, segments and cards. No browser. npm run test:e2e node tests/e2e/run-e2e.mjs: drives tests/fixtures/player.html in Chromium with the Playwright library. npm test Unit tests, then end-to-end tests. npm run build:docs Copy the dist/ bundles and the testdata/ media into src_docs/md/, and stamp cache-busting hashes into the demo pages.

dist/ is not committed. The prepack script runs npm run build, so npm pack and npm publish always ship fresh bundles.

docs.title: The build.sh script
docs.text:
The root build.sh accepts one target:

Command Steps ./build.sh or ./build.sh all Unit tests, bundles, demo assets, documentation site. ./build.sh package Unit tests and bundles. ./build.sh docs Bundles, demo assets (npm run build:docs), then src_docs/build.sh.

docs.title: Documentation site
docs.text:
The site you are reading is built with ProperDocs and the MaterialX theme.

  • Markdown sources and the demo pages live in src_docs/md/.
  • The configuration is src_docs/mkdocs.yml.
  • src_docs/build.sh runs a strict build into docs/, which GitHub Pages serves at https://vexy.dev/vexy-vlip-js/. Do not edit docs/ by hand: each build replaces it.
  • src_docs/build.sh serve starts a live preview on http://127.0.0.1:8000.

To change a demo page, edit its file in src_docs/md/ and rebuild.

The .github/workflows/docs.yml workflow rebuilds the bundles, the demo assets and the site on every push to main that touches the sources, and commits the updated docs/ folder.

After a docs build, node scripts/verify-docs.mjs loads each demo page from docs/ in Chromium and checks that the player starts and shows cards.

docs.title: Continuous integration
docs.text: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs on pushes to main and on pull requests: it installs dependencies, runs the unit tests, builds the bundles, installs Chromium and runs the end-to-end tests.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text:
The git tag is the source of the version number.

  • From a GitHub Release. Publishing a release for a vX.Y.Z tag runs .github/workflows/publish.yml. It writes the tag's version into package.json, runs the unit tests, builds the bundles and runs npm publish --provenance --access public. It needs npm trusted publishing or an NPM_TOKEN repository secret.
  • From a workstation. ./publish.sh runs uvx gitnextver to tag the next version, copies that version into package.json and the version export in src/index.js, builds, and publishes to npm. ./publish.sh --dryrun packs the current version without publishing.

docs.title: Reference media
docs.text: testdata/ holds the media the tests and demos use. testdata/playlines.mp4 and testdata/playlines.vtt come from scripts/capture-playlines.mjs, which records the Vexy Playlines editor with Playwright, and scripts/transcode-playlines.sh, which transcodes the recording.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: vexy-vlip-js is published to npm under the name vexy-vlip-js. It has no runtime dependencies. You can install it from npm or load it from a CDN with no build step.

docs.title: Install from npm
docs.text:
Prerequisites: Node.js and npm. The package declares "engines": { "node": ">=18.0.0" }.

  1. Add the package to your project:

    npm i vexy-vlip-js

  2. Import the entry point you need (see Package entry points):

    import { VexyVlip } from "vexy-vlip-js";

The package ships both the unbundled ESM source (src/) and two prebuilt bundles (dist/vexy-vlip.element.js and dist/vexy-vlip.global.js).

docs.title: Package entry points
docs.text:
The exports map in package.json defines these import paths:

Import path File Effect vexy-vlip-js src/index.js Exports the VexyVlip class and helpers. Does not register <vexy-vlip>. vexy-vlip-js/element src/element.js Registers the <vexy-vlip> custom element as a side effect. vexy-vlip-js/styles src/styles.js The stylesheet as a string plus injectStyles(). vexy-vlip-js/dist/* dist/* The prebuilt bundles.

The unpkg and jsdelivr fields both point at dist/vexy-vlip.global.js, so a bare CDN URL for the package serves the classic-script build.

docs.title: Load from a CDN
docs.text:
No install is needed. Pin a version so a new release cannot break your page: @1.0.0 is exact, @1 is the latest 1.x, and no version means the latest release.

Web ComponentClassic globalES module 
<!-- Registers <vexy-vlip> -->
<script type="module"
  src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/vexy-vlip-js@1/dist/vexy-vlip.element.js"></script>

<vexy-vlip src="demo.mp4" track="demo.vtt" mode="stepped" controls></vexy-vlip>

<!-- window.VexyVlip + <vexy-vlip>; the bare URL resolves to the global build -->
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/vexy-vlip-js@1"></script>

<script type="module">
  import { VexyVlip } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/vexy-vlip-js@1/src/index.js";
</script>

unpkg accepts the same paths. jsDelivr also serves an auto-bundled module at …/vexy-vlip-js@1/+esm.

Production embeds

Use a version-pinned jsDelivr or unpkg URL in production. The bundles on this documentation site, such as https://vexy.dev/vexy-vlip-js/vexy-vlip.element.js, are unversioned and always track the latest deployed site. They suit demos, not production pages.

docs.title: Prepare your media
docs.text:
Vexy Vlip plays any video the browser can play. For the best result:

  1. Encode H.264/AAC MP4 for broad browser support.

  2. Move the MP4 metadata to the start of the file so playback can begin immediately:

    ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -movflags +faststart out.mp4

  3. If you use eased travel (easing other than linear), encode with a short GOP so seeking stays smooth.

  4. Serve the .vtt file from a URL the page can fetch(). A cross-origin track needs CORS headers, because the player downloads it with fetch.

Next: Quick start.

docs.title: Options and attributes
docs.text:
You configure a player with an options object passed to the VexyVlip constructor, or with attributes on <vexy-vlip>. Both routes set the same values; the defaults come from the exported DEFAULTS object in src/player.js.

import { VexyVlip, DEFAULTS } from "vexy-vlip-js";

console.log(DEFAULTS.mode);       // "continuous"
new VexyVlip(stage, { src: "demo.mp4", track: "demo.vtt", mode: "stepped" });

<vexy-vlip src="demo.mp4" track="demo.vtt" mode="stepped"></vexy-vlip>

docs.title: Attribute rules
docs.text:
• Attribute names are the kebab-case form of the option: autoFit becomes auto-fit, startSegment becomes start-segment.
  • The video title uses the attribute video-title. The plain title attribute also works, but it also sets the browser's native tooltip.
  • Boolean attributes follow HTML semantics: presence means true. The values "false" and "0" mean false. An absent attribute uses the default.
  • Every attribute is observed. Changes to mode, easing, muted, loop and poster apply to the running player. Any other change rebuilds the player so the new value takes effect.

docs.title: Media and playback
docs.text: Option Attribute Type Default Notes src src string "" Video URL. track track string "" WebVTT URL, downloaded with fetch(). vtt vtt string "" Inline WebVTT text, used instead of track. mode mode "continuous" | "stepped" "continuous" Playback mode. Any other value means continuous. easing easing "linear" | "ease-in" | "ease-out" | "ease-in-out" "linear" Travel between stops in stepped mode. linear uses native playback with audio. controls controls boolean true Show the control bar. In stepped mode the bar shows the step dots only. autoplay autoplay boolean false In continuous mode, start playing when ready and skip the Start screen. loop loop boolean false Loop the video. Applies in continuous mode only. muted muted boolean false Start muted. Browsers usually allow autoplay only when muted. poster poster string "" Poster image URL. startAt start-at number 0 Initial time in seconds. startSegment start-segment number null Open on this card index, already positioned, with no Start screen. keyboard keyboard boolean true Enable keyboard shortcuts on the player. sanitize sanitize boolean false Filter JSON html cards. See Authoring cards.

docs.title: Stepped-mode interface
docs.text: Option Attribute Type Default Notes overlay overlay boolean true Dim the video behind a resting card. nav nav boolean true Show the in-card Next button (and Back when back is on). back back boolean false Show the in-card ← Back button. prev() and the Left key work either way. closable closable boolean true Show the in-card ×, which switches to continuous mode and resumes playback. counter counter boolean false Show an n/total step counter in the card footer. dots dots boolean true Show the step-dots bar.

docs.title: Labels and title
docs.text: Option Attribute Default Notes nextLabel next-label "Next →" In-card Next button. prevLabel prev-label "←" In-card Back button. startLabel start-label "Start →" Start button over the dimmed first frame. replayLabel replay-label "Replay ↻" Replay button shown after the video ends. title video-title (or title) "" Video title. Shown above the Start/Replay button and in a small top-left bar during playback. titleBar title-bar true When a title is set, show the top-left title bar during playback.

docs.title: Card sizing
docs.text:
Option Attribute Type Default Notes autoFit auto-fit boolean true Grow cards to fit their text, then scale the whole card down if it still overflows. minScale min-scale number 0.4 Smallest scale factor auto-fit may apply. maxWidth max-width number 72 Grow limit as a percentage of the player width. Also sets --vv-card-max-width.

Auto-fit keeps the Next button on one line, scales around the card's anchor so the placement is preserved, and runs again when the player is resized or enters full screen.

docs.title: Theme shortcuts
docs.text:
Each of these options writes a CSS custom property on the player root. See Theming for the full list of properties.

Option Attribute Sets cardBg card-bg --vv-card-bg and --vv-card-bg-stepped cardFg card-fg --vv-card-fg nextBg next-bg --vv-next-bg nextFg next-fg --vv-next-fg nextBorder next-border --vv-next-border startBg start-bg --vv-start-bg startFg start-fg --vv-start-fg titleColor title-color --vv-title-fg titleBg title-bg --vv-title-bg titleSize title-size --vv-title-size font font --vv-card-font dim dim --vv-overlay-bg. A number from 0 to 1 means black at that opacity; any other value is used as a CSS colour.

docs.title: Class-only options
docs.text: Option Default Notes injectStyles true Insert the player stylesheet once into the document <head>. The Web Component sets this to false and puts the styles in its shadow root instead. onReady, onStop, … — Callback for each event: on plus the event name with a capital first letter. It receives (detail, player). See Events.

docs.title: Start and Replay screens
docs.text:
Before playback, both modes show the dimmed first frame with a Start → button. Clicking it, clicking the frame, or pressing Space begins playback: stepped mode advances to the first card, continuous mode removes the dim and plays. The Start screen is skipped when autoplay is on in continuous mode, or when startSegment is set.

After the video ends, the same screen returns with Replay ↻, unless the video is looping.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: This page builds a stepped explainer from one video and a three-cue WebVTT file. It uses the <vexy-vlip> Web Component, which needs no JavaScript of your own.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A video file, here demo.mp4.
  • A web server for the page. The player downloads the track with fetch(), so opening the HTML file directly from disk (file://) may fail.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Create demo.vtt next to the video:

    WEBVTT

step-1
00:02.000 --> 00:03.500
This is a **plain-text** card near the bottom.

step-2
00:04.000 --> 00:05.500 position:18% line:30% size:34% align:start
A card placed top-left via native WebVTT cue settings.

step-3
00:06.000 --> 00:07.500
{ "text": "A JSON card with a custom backdrop.", "x": 50, "y": 50, "anchor": "center", "bg": "#10243a", "fg": "#eaf2ff", "radius": 16 }

    Each cue is one card. step-1 uses the default placement, step-2 uses WebVTT cue settings, and step-3 is a JSON card with its own colours.

  2. Create index.html that loads the element build and places the player:

    <!doctype html>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<script type="module"
  src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/vexy-vlip-js@1/dist/vexy-vlip.element.js"></script>

<vexy-vlip src="demo.mp4" track="demo.vtt" mode="stepped" muted
           video-title="My first explainer"></vexy-vlip>

  3. Serve the folder, for example with npx vite or python3 -m http.server, and open the page.

  4. Click Start →. The video plays to 2 s, pauses, dims, and shows the first card. Click the card, the video, or Next →, or press Space, to play to the next card. After the last card the next advance plays to the end of the video, and a Replay ↻ button appears.

docs.title: The same player from JavaScript
Inline tracks
docs.text:
Instead of a URL, pass the WebVTT text directly with the vtt option (or the vtt attribute). The player then skips the network request:

new VexyVlip(stage, {
  src: "demo.mp4",
  vtt: "WEBVTT\n\n00:01.000 --> 00:03.000\nHello",
});

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Learn the full cue syntax in Authoring cards.
  • Change colours and labels with Options and attributes or Theming.

docs.title: Theming
docs.text: Every visual setting of the player is a CSS custom property declared on the player root, the element with the class vexy-vlip. Per-card JSON fields such as bg, fg and shadow override these values with inline styles on single cards.

docs.title: Three ways to set a property
docs.text:
1. Theme options or attributes. Options such as cardBg or attributes such as card-bg write the matching property as an inline style on the player root. This works the same for the class and for <vexy-vlip>. See Theme shortcuts.

    <vexy-vlip src="demo.mp4" track="demo.vtt" mode="stepped"
           card-bg="#10243a" card-fg="#eaf2ff" dim="0.5"></vexy-vlip>

  2. Your own stylesheet (class build). The class injects its stylesheet into <head> at runtime, after your own styles, and declares the defaults on .vexy-vlip. Use a more specific selector so your values win:

    #stage.vexy-vlip {
  --vv-card-bg: #10243a;
  --vv-card-fg: #eaf2ff;
  --vv-card-radius: 8px;
}

  3. Inline style on the container (class build).

    stage.style.setProperty("--vv-accent", "#e4572e");
new VexyVlip(stage, { src: "demo.mp4", track: "demo.vtt" });

Web Component

<vexy-vlip> keeps its stylesheet in a shadow root, and that stylesheet declares the defaults on the inner .vexy-vlip element. Custom properties set on the <vexy-vlip> host are therefore replaced by those defaults. Use the theme attributes to style the element.

docs.title: Card properties
docs.text: Property Default Controls --vv-card-bg #ffffff Card background --vv-card-bg-stepped var(--vv-card-bg) Card background in stepped mode --vv-card-fg #1d2430 Card text colour --vv-card-font inherit Card font --vv-card-padding 20px 24px Card padding --vv-card-radius 16px Card corner radius --vv-card-border 0 Card border --vv-card-shadow 0 12px 38px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.34) Card shadow --vv-card-max-width 72% Largest card width; the maxWidth option also sets it --vv-accent #2f6fed Link colour and default active-dot colour

docs.title: Buttons
docs.text: Property Default Controls --vv-next-bg #ffffff In-card Next button background (outlined pill by default) --vv-next-fg #1d2430 Next button text colour --vv-next-border rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.82) Next button border --vv-start-bg #1d2430 Start button background when a title is set --vv-start-fg #ffffff Start button text colour when a title is set --vv-close-fg var(--vv-card-fg) Close (×) button colour

docs.title: Overlay, dots and controls
docs.text: Property Default Controls --vv-overlay-bg rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.7) Dim layer behind a resting card or the Start/Replay screen --vv-dot rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.45) Step-dot colour --vv-dot-active var(--vv-accent) Active step-dot colour --vv-controls-bg rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.55) Control bar background

docs.title: Title bar
docs.text:
These properties have no declaration on the root; the stylesheet uses the listed fallback until you set them.

Property Fallback Controls --vv-title-fg rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.92) Top-left title colour --vv-title-bg rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.45) Top-left title background --vv-title-size 13px Top-left title font size --vv-title-padding 4px 10px Top-left title padding --vv-title-radius 7px Top-left title corner radius --vv-title-margin 10px 12px Offset from the corner

docs.title: Class names for your own CSS
docs.text:
The player root also carries data-mode="continuous" or data-mode="stepped". Cards are .vexy-vlip__card elements inside .vexy-vlip__cards; a visible card also has .vexy-vlip__card--in. A JSON card's class field adds your own class names to its card element.

/* Class build: style a card tagged { "class": "tip" } in the VTT file. */
.vexy-vlip .vexy-vlip__card.tip { --vv-card-radius: 4px; }

docs.title: Reduced motion
docs.text: When the system requests reduced motion (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce), the stylesheet removes the card slide transforms and the button and dot transitions.
